My First Solo Dinner in here :)
Aug 2023 • Solo
First and foremost, I would like to express my gratitude to the kitchen for preparing such delicious dishes tonight.

The presence of an Asian fusion on the menu brings about a sense of harmony; however, the predominant taste leans towards Thai cuisine.

To start off my dinner, I indulged in two portions of beef and shrimp dumplings. The shrimp dumplings had a golden crust, a chewy texture, and firm, sweet shrimp meat (although the sauce was quite spicy for my liking). On the other hand, the beef dumplings had a chewy shell made from Japanese rice flour, tender beef, and a non-spicy sesame sauce. Interestingly, even when eaten with the spicy sauce, the shrimp dumplings still proved to be a delightful and delicious choice due to their lack of spiciness.

Being a fan of fried foods, I found myself torn between ordering fried chicken or fried squid, so I decided to have both for the purpose of comparison. Both dishes boasted a crispy golden fried dough crust. The fried chicken had tender meat, accompanied by a sweet and salty dipping sauce that was not spicy. As for the fried squid, it showcased the tenderness of seafood complemented by a sweet and creamy sauce. These shared dishes are particularly suitable for groups of two or more people, allowing them to be enjoyed together. I found the fried squid preferable, as the fried chicken tended to be a bit dry and lacked excitement when consumed alone.

Due to its embodiment of the typical Thai taste, I opted to order Tom Yum once again. The broth possessed a perfect consistency, an eye-catching color, an enticing aroma derived from the herbs, and a delicate balance of sweetness, acidity, and lightness. Additionally, it featured 3 firm and sweet tiger prawns paired with Vietnamese straw mushrooms.

Finally, concluding the meal with the most delectable dessert on the menu, the Banana Crepe, left an indescribable sense of excitement. The soft crust, fragrant bananas, the harmonious blend of sweet and salty notes from the caramel sauce, the richness of coconut milk, and the sweetness of coconut cream contributed to a cake that was far from dry. Each bite resulted in a harmonious fusion of flavors that evoked pure happiness.

As someone who enjoys a quieter environment, especially during the early days of the week, I truly appreciate a space that is not overly noisy. This tranquility allows me to fully savor and relish a delicious meal.

HCMC’s finest restaurant & bar (we visited).... 

We visited The Racha Room on our final night in HCMC and it proved to be 100% the right choice for us. We both agreed it was the best restaurant and bar we’d visited (anywhere) in a long time. Here’s why:

- LOCATION: Cool set up for a restaurant that’s also a fab place to have cocktails, with a dedicated bar, if you are just looking for a drinks’ stop. It might be a bit loud for an intimate dinner but we certainly enjoyed the vibe. A great place for anyone to visit- lots of big groups seemed to visit that night. Worth booking. 

- COCKTAILS: We loved the cocktails, broadly priced between 170-240 VND. Try The Racha (see photo). Delicious! They also seem to have Happy Hour 5-8pm, though we missed it. 

- FOOD: They serve snacks and light bites, medium and larger plates, as well as sides. We had some delicious chicken and mint dumplings, chicken satay skewers, followed by prawn and mango Massaman curry with a side of coconut rice and some delicious crispy sweetcorn fritters. That proved just a nice amount to share between two people. 

- SERVICE: Service was excellent and everyone very friendly, asking if we has enough drinks etc at a nice pace. We gave our feedback about our experience and our waiter seemed very pleased at the end. 

Overall, a strong 5/5 for us. Our bill was about 2m VND ((£65/70 UK) but well worth the pricier side if eating out in HCMC. 

It’s a must visit place if you are looking for great food, great cocktails and a chilled but not too dressy/ pretentious place to spend an evening. 

Definitely, our HCMC’s finest 👍. Absolutely A.M.A.Z.I.N.G!..

Disappointing Service
Oct 2017 • Couples
For reference, I've lived in Saigon for over 3 years, and have visited many restaurants, including Stoker and Relish & Sons, both of which are owned by the same company (Tribe Hospitality) as The Racha Room. I've also reviewed many Saigon restaurants on TA.

We visited today for a late lunch, and will not return. It is not often I would say this about a restaurant. First, when I ordered the salmon sashimi, the waiter stopped me and said in an almost condescending tone, "That is raw fish." My husband was a bit taken aback by the "mansplaining" and was offended. I mostly ignored it, but felt it strange that in 2017, waiters would think they need to explain this word to women. 

Later, I saw the waiter pouring glasses on an empty table with iced tea and he stopped to get a new pitcher near our table. I asked for some tra da as well. He paused, gave me an impatient look like I was inconveniencing him, and said, "In a moment," and went back to the empty table, filling glasses there before coming to give us some. In an empty restaurant, this was just a bit strange. Like the empty table was more of a priority than customers already at the restaurant.

When we were close to being done, a waitress came and asked if we were finished with our main dish. We were, and said she could take it. She then took ALL of our dishes, including the small plates we were eating off of, although we were not finished with our rice and there was still rice in the serving bowl we were going to eat. It happened so fast, we couldn't ask for our plates back, as she had stacked them on top of the dirty main dish. We had barely finished eating when this had happened. I guess it was time for us to go! We were there for no more than 30 minutes total.

We asked for the bill, and it was brought to us by a 3rd waitstaff. No smile, no, "Here is your bill, sir," no niceties. She was downright dour. We paid and determined if we should ask for a manager, and decided that before leaving a review online, the right thing to do was talk with a manager in the restaurant to share our experience.

Unfortunately the manager on duty was waiter #1 who felt like he needed to explain what sashimi was and put the needs of an empty table ahead of ours. He did explain that some people don't know that sashimi is raw fish and wanted to be sure that we knew. He also said he was setting up for a meeting and needed to pour the tea for that group. Both were reasonable explanations, but the vibe was off. He then proceeded to talk over us when we tried to share how we felt the service wasn't fitting of Tribe hospitality.

In conclusion, the waitstaff was unpleasant, which is not normal for Saigon. The manager was not up to par in comparison to those at Stoker/Relish & Sons. We left having paid 1.1 million for a sashimi appetizer, 3 dumplings, 6 grilled prawns and 2 cocktails. Had the service been great, we'd have felt better about the price, but we pay for a good experience as well as for good food. 

As is, I'd say don't bother. If you are a 30-40's couple that enjoys trying new restaurants or finer dining in Saigon, keep looking.

Sensational last night in Ho Chi Minh
Apr 2017 • Family
For our last night in Vietnam we wanted something a bit special and the Racha Room was perfect. It is a very trendy bar and restaurant with a great vibe from the minute you walk in. It is a bit of East meets West, and we later found out it is backed by some Australians, so don't go there expecting the authentic Vietnam experience! It is Vietnamese inspired for sure, but will also suit those that might be missing home. Service was exceptional, the food and drink was perfect, and we felt like staying long after dinner was over.
